I am a doctoral researcher at the Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering (ITEE), University of Oulu, specialising in artificial intelligence and remote sensing for hydrology modelling. My work focuses on developing deep learning methods that extract snow and water characteristics from multi-modal satellite imagery — combining Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical, and DEM data to build climate-resilient runoff prediction models.

139→

My academic journey spans multiple continents: a BSc and MSc in electrical engineering and communication systems from Bahir Dar University, Ethiopia, followed by an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degree (IPCV) across the University of Bordeaux (France), Autonomous University of Madrid (Spain), and Pázmány Péter Catholic University (Hungary). Research visits to RISE Sweden (Gothenburg) and University of Florida TREC have broadened my expertise to Nordic snow monitoring and multi-sensor tropical remote sensing.

140→

I am co-organising the HydroImaging Workshop at IEEE ICIP 2026 in Tampere, Finland, and actively contribute to the growing GeoAI research community through publications, conference presentations, and open-source tools.
